title: Wyoming's At-Large Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Wyoming's at-large U.S. House seat is an open-seat contest following incumbent Republican Rep. Harriet Hageman's decision to run for the U.S. Senate instead of seeking re-election. A large and competitive Republican primary field has emerged, including Secretary of State Chuck Gray, former state Superintendent Jillian Balow, state Senate President Bo Biteman, and businessman Reid Rasner, among others. The Democratic primary features former state Senator and minority leader Lisa Kinney and first-time candidate Elena Del Real. Wyoming's at-large district is considered a safely Republican seat, and the winner of the August 18 Republican primary is heavily favored in the November general election.

candidates.name: Jillian Balow
candidates.summary: Jillian Balow is a former Wyoming Superintendent of Public Instruction (2015–2022) and former Virginia Superintendent of Public Instruction (2022–2023), appointed by Governor Glenn Youngkin. A Gillette native, she was elected statewide twice in Wyoming and has focused her campaign on education, local control, and conservative governance. Balow holds a BA from the University of Wyoming and an MEd from Regis University.

candidates.name: Bo Biteman
candidates.summary: Bo Biteman is the President of the Wyoming Senate (2025–present), representing the 21st Senate district since 2019. He has been a prominent conservative voice in the state legislature and is now seeking the open U.S. House seat, emphasizing his legislative leadership and experience in state government. Biteman's campaign focuses on energy independence, conservative fiscal policy, and Wyoming's interests in Washington.

candidates.name: Reid Rasner
candidates.summary: Reid Rasner is a Wyoming businessman who previously ran for the U.S. Senate in 2024, finishing second in the Republican primary. He is now seeking the open U.S. House seat, leveraging his prior campaign experience and personal wealth to build a well-funded operation. Rasner's platform centers on economic growth, border security, and conservative principles.

candidates.name: Steve Friess
candidates.summary: Steve Friess is a conservative activist and the son of late prominent Republican donor Foster Friess. He has been active in Wyoming conservative circles and is running for the open U.S. House seat with a focus on limited government, conservative social values, and supporting President Trump's America First agenda. Friess was polling at 10% in a May 2026 Republican primary poll.

candidates.name: Lisa F. Kinney
candidates.summary: Lisa F. Kinney is a former Wyoming State Senator who served for a decade, including as Minority Leader, and is the presumptive Democratic nominee for Wyoming's at-large U.S. House seat. An attorney, former librarian, and former president of the Albany County Chamber of Commerce, she runs on an affordability-focused platform that includes cutting payroll taxes for lower earners and raising taxes on higher incomes — an approach she calls 'Congressional Robin Hood.' Kinney emphasizes that her campaign is built on input from Wyoming professionals and residents rather than wealthy donors or national party endorsements.

candidates.summary: Shawn Johnson is the Libertarian Party candidate for Wyoming's at-large U.S. House seat, and is a former vice mayor of Casper, Wyoming. He enters a race where the general election is expected to be heavily Republican-leaning, offering voters a third-party alternative focused on libertarian principles of limited government and individual liberty.

forecast.rationale: Wyoming's at-large House seat is an open-seat contest following Rep. Hageman's Senate run. The district is described as safely Republican, and the winner of the competitive August 18 Republican primary is heavily favored in November. No general-election polling exists in the data — the two listed polls (Fabrizio, Lee & Associates and Peak Insights) are Republican primary polls with empty matchup arrays and provide no general-election head-to-head numbers. The Democratic nominee (likely former state Sen. Lisa Kinney) is a credible candidate, but Wyoming's partisan lean is extreme: the state has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. House since 2008, and Republicans typically win by 35–40 percentage points in federal races. A Libertarian candidate is also running but is not competitive. Confidence is medium because the Republican nominee is not yet determined and no general-election polling is available to validate the margin estimate, though the structural partisan advantage is unambiguous.
